title: The repo-root wrangler manifest is the single declaration of the Worker's deploy shape
description: A `wrangler.toml` (or the equivalent `wrangler.jsonc`) at the repo root is the sole declaration of the Worker's deploy shape. It carries the Worker `name`, the entrypoint `main`, a pinned `compatibility_date`, any `compatibility_flags`, and every non-secret binding the runtime needs: KV namespaces, D1 databases, R2 buckets, Durable Object namespaces, static-assets binding, and non-secret environment variables. Secret bindings are NOT declared in the manifest (wrangler 4.x has no `[secrets]` block, no `secrets.required[]` list, and no empty-value binding entry for secrets); the vendor treats every env-accessor reference from Worker code as an implicit secret binding declaration and enforces its presence at deploy time by refusing `wrangler deploy` when a referenced secret has not been set on the target. Nothing outside the manifest may configure a non-secret binding at deploy time; a non-secret binding referenced from Worker code but absent from the manifest is a build refusal (an implicitly-referenced secret is caught by the vendor's own pre-deploy refusal instead). No secret VALUE ever appears in the manifest.
rationale: A scattered deploy configuration is the failure mode this blueprint exists to end. If bindings are declared in ad-hoc scripts, CI environment blocks, or hand-edited before deploy, no one knows what the deployed Worker actually looks like. A single manifest at a known path makes the deploy shape legible to humans, to CI gates, to the vendor's deploy step, and to review of every change that touches a binding.
